The seaward half of every plant on one bank dried to dead brown and brittle, the sheltered half still bright green, the two halves meeting in one sharp straight edge.
A whole slope of pink flower heads all leaning exactly the same way, as though a single comb had been pulled through the hillside from sea to land.
One tight clump of flowers in full bloom growing out of a crack right at the edge of the ground with nothing at all underneath it, open water far below.
The tops of every plant cut level at exactly one height so the bank reads as a flat green table, the bare rock poking up through it in places.
Bright orange crusty lichen on one slab so vivid it out-colours every flower growing next to it.
A single bead of water sitting in the exact centre of one flower, round and still, acting as a lens over the yellow stamens beneath it.
A hollow in the bare rock holding a small pool of standing seawater, two pale petals floating on its surface without touching each other.
A ring of taller, greener, denser flowers growing in the exact wind-shadow of one boulder, the ground on the boulder's other side carrying almost nothing.
Last year's stems bleached bone-white by salt standing upright among this year's hot-pink flowers, thin as wire against the green.
One flower head turned to face inland while every other head on the same slope faces the same opposite direction.
A single stem bent right over by the wind so its flower head touches the surface of the rock and stays there, pressed flat.
A tuft of white down no bigger than one of the flower heads beside it caught on a spine of dead stem, held perfectly still against the moving air around it.
One white flower head still carrying a small pinch of hail in the gap between its petals, unmelted, sitting there like coarse salt.
A straight brown band of dried dead leaf running right across every plant at exactly one height, the living green starting again sharply above it.
A crack in the rock packed with old white shell fragments instead of soil, a plant rooted directly into the grit and flowering regardless.
A scatter of tiny white barnacle shells and fine shell grit sitting among the flower stems on a flat plate of rock, carried up from far below by the wind.
A patch of flowers growing in a shallow dip that is noticeably greener and lusher than everything surrounding it, the fog draining into it and staying.
Grass growing along the full length of a single crack in the rock in one straight line, no bend in it anywhere from one end to the other.
A slab of rock that has already parted from the main ground by a narrow open gap, a plant rooted in the gap and flowering from the moving piece.
A pool of shadow thrown by one cloud lying right across the middle of the slope so precisely that the flowers on one side are lit and the other side is dark.
A thin crust of dried white salt left in the low centre of a leaf after the seawater that carried it evaporated, the outline of the original drop still legible.
Two colours of lichen on one rock, the orange crustose kind and a pale grey-green flaky kind, meeting in one hard irregular border with neither overlapping the other.
A small wedge of bare dark peaty soil exposed where a chunk of turf has peeled back at the very edge, the layered roots visible in section beneath the green.
The grass at the edge broken off short and fraying into individual hanging rootlets where the soil has fallen away, each rootlet pale against the open water beyond.
A loose pile of flat broken stone fragments on a bare patch between the flowers, each piece stacked at a slight angle as the freeze and thaw left them, no two pieces parallel.
